novelty.justification: The core hypothesis is that dominant-language intermediate tokens appear "not because computation is dominant-language-based, but because the unembedding is dominant-language-biased," and that a "per-language calibrated unembedding" will reveal a more language-neutral code; its novelty route is therefore a readout-bias mechanism and language-specific measurement rather than merely a new multilingual setting. Searches around "multilingual calibrated logit lens," "language-specific tuned lens," and "logit lens English bias" identify Indic-TunedLens (2026) as the closest work: it already learns target-language affine transformations to decode multilingual intermediate states more faithfully, while the general premise that raw logit-lens decoding is distorted by layerwise representational mismatch comes from Belrose et al.'s Tuned Lens. Recasting English-centric logit-lens findings specifically as an unembedding artifact adds a distinct prediction, but moving from those calibrated-lens methods to this claim is a natural extension rather than a new core measurement paradigm, and the proposed method substantially overlaps existing work.
